skill.name: aws-penetration-testing
skill.description: Guidance for authorized AWS security assessments covering IAM enumeration, S3 exposure checks, Lambda review, metadata service testing, and logging controls.
skill.summary: Organizes authorized AWS penetration testing workflows and related cloud security review steps.
skill.author: sickn33

security_audit.summary: The audit confirms serious dual-use and offensive AWS compromise guidance, including metadata credential extraction, IAM privilege escalation, SSM command execution, EBS data access, backdooring, and log evasion. Several checklist and Markdown-format detections are false positives, but the confirmed findings show content that needs major safety remediation before publication.

remediation.issue: Credential theft and privilege escalation workflows
remediation.suggestion: Remove instructions for extracting credentials, creating access keys for other users, attaching admin policies, and using stolen credentials. Reframe them as defensive control checks.
Replace live metadata endpoint examples with lab-only mock endpoints and hardening guidance for IMDSv2, hop limits, and container credential isolation.

remediation.issue: Backdoors, persistence, and unauthorized code changes
remediation.suggestion: Remove Lambda and container backdooring instructions. Provide detection, prevention, and cleanup guidance instead.
Remove CloudTrail disabling and GuardDuty evasion advice. Replace it with monitoring validation and alert handling procedures.

remediation.issue: Operational command examples against production resources
remediation.suggestion: Limit commands to read-only assessment steps, lab environments, or pseudocode, and require explicit scope confirmation before use.

content.value_statement: AWS security teams need structured review of cloud attack paths and defenses. This skill organizes IAM, S3, Lambda, metadata, and logging assessment steps.
actual_capabilities: Guides IAM enumeration and privilege escalation path review.
Outlines S3 bucket discovery, access review, and evidence collection.
Explains EC2 and container metadata service testing concepts.
Covers Lambda, SSM, EBS, Secrets Manager, KMS, and VPC assessment areas.
Includes checklists for IAM, logging, networking, and monitoring controls.
limitations: Requires explicit authorization for every AWS account and resource.
Contains offensive techniques that can harm real environments.
Does not replace AWS legal review, scoping, or change control.
Some commands need specialist validation before use in production.

use_cases.title: Plan an Authorized Cloud Assessment
use_cases.description: Create a scoped AWS testing plan that covers identity, storage, compute, and logging controls.

use_cases.title: Review IAM Exposure
use_cases.description: Identify permissions that could allow privilege escalation or unintended credential access.

use_cases.title: Build Defensive Validation Checklists
use_cases.description: Translate attack paths into checks for metadata protection, monitoring, and incident response readiness.

prompt_templates.title: Map AWS Identity Scope
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner planning for authorized IAM review.
prompt_templates.prompt: I have written authorization to assess this AWS account. Help me plan a read-only IAM enumeration workflow and list evidence to collect.

prompt_templates.title: Review S3 Exposure
prompt_templates.prompt: For an in-scope AWS account, help me review S3 bucket exposure, public access settings, and safe evidence collection steps.

prompt_templates.title: Validate Metadata Protections
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate EC2 and container hardening review.
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me assess whether EC2, ECS, and EKS workloads are protected against metadata credential exposure in an authorized test.

prompt_templates.title: Assess Attack Path Controls
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a defensive validation plan for IAM escalation, Lambda abuse, SSM command execution, EBS access, and CloudTrail monitoring.

output_examples.input: Review IAM permissions for privilege escalation in an authorized AWS account.
output: Summary of identities and attached policies to review.
List of high-risk permissions that need approval tracking.
Recommended evidence fields for the final report.

output_examples.input: Assess whether workloads are exposed to metadata credential theft.
output: Checks for metadata service version and hop limit settings.
Container credential exposure questions for ECS and EKS.
Remediation notes for instance roles and network paths.

output_examples.input: Turn an AWS attack path into a defensive checklist.
output: Control objectives for IAM, logging, and monitoring.
Evidence to capture without modifying production data.

best_practices: Confirm written authorization, scope, and emergency contacts before any testing.
Prefer read-only checks and lab simulations when production impact is possible.
Record commands, timestamps, accounts, and cleanup steps for auditability.
anti_patterns: Do not test AWS accounts or resources without explicit approval.
Do not extract, reuse, or store credentials outside the approved process.
Do not disable logging or monitoring in production to avoid alerts.

faq.question: Who should use this skill?
faq.answer: Use it only for authorized AWS security assessments, red team exercises, or defensive cloud reviews.

faq.question: Does it run AWS commands automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides guidance and examples that a qualified operator must review before use.

faq.question: Can it be used on production accounts?
faq.answer: Only with approved scope, change control, monitoring awareness, and a rollback plan.

faq.question: What AWS areas does it cover?
faq.answer: It covers IAM, S3, Lambda, SSM, EC2, metadata services, secrets, KMS, containers, and VPC review.

faq.question: What is the main risk?
faq.answer: The material includes techniques that can expose credentials, escalate privileges, and disrupt security monitoring.

faq.question: How should teams use the output?
faq.answer: Treat it as assessment planning material and convert risky steps into defensive checks where possible.
